FXUS63 KIWX 081132
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
632 AM EST Sun Nov 8 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Becoming breezy today with highs in the mid-upper 50s.

- Remaining dry into Monday and Tuesday with gradual warming.

- Trending cooler late Wednesday through Friday with chances 
  for rain, mainly late Wednesday afternoon into Thursday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 217 AM EST Sun Nov 8 2026

Low level height field tightens today in response to a system 
passing off to the north with diurnal mixing supporting a few 
late morning/afternoon westerly gusts up to 25-30 mph. This 
system does force a weak front through later today into tonight.
No threat for rain however given the dry column and overall 
weak ascent. Low amplitude west-northwest flow aloft persists 
otherwise into Tuesday with quiet wx and gradual warming. 

A deep upper level trough remains on target to dig into the Eastern 
US late Wednesday through Saturday with deepening northerly flow 
and colder temperatures. The last several model cycles have been 
farther north with the leading wave and sfc reflection Wednesday 
afternoon-night with increasing prospects for a period of rain.
This low exits east into Thursday and Friday with colder 
northerly flow in its wake. Rounds of mid level dpva and deep 
northerly flow with 850 mb temps down to near -5C looking should
support a healthy long lake axis response during this time into
far nw IN and possibly sw MI. The lake modified mixed layer 
could cool just enough for the first snowflakes to mix in 
further inland later Thursday night.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z MONDAY/...
Issued at 629 AM EST Sun Nov 8 2026

VFR conditions expected this TAF period with a few diurnal 
clouds around 2000-2500 ft later this morning into the
afternoon. Gusty westerly winds with gusts around 25 kts after
14-15z Sun.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.

     Monday for LMZ046.

spc.summary: Strong to locally severe thunderstorms may occur today across parts of south Texas. Isolated damaging winds and perhaps a brief tornado appear possible.
spc.text:
SPC AC 081614

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1014 AM CST Sun Nov 08 2026

   Valid 081630Z - 091200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS TODAY ALONG THE
   MIDDLE-LOWER TEXAS COAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Strong to locally severe thunderstorms may occur today across parts
   of south Texas. Isolated damaging winds and perhaps a brief tornado
   appear possible.

   ...Middle-lower TX coast today...
   A midlevel low over northern Mexico will drift slowly eastward and
   weaken through the period.  At the surface, a baroclinic zone along
   the middle-lower TX coast will provide a focus for thunderstorms
   rooted at the surface, where boundary-layer dewpoints will remain
   near 70 F.  Per the 12z observed soundings/VWPs/model forecasts,
   deep-layer vertical shear will remain sufficient for some embedded
   rotating storms, with the relatively stronger low-level
   shear/hodograph curvature expected along the north edge of the
   surface-based buoyancy with a small MCV just south of CRP.  Poor
   midlevel lapse rates will temper the overall severe threat, though
   an isolated, weak tornado and/or localized wind damage will be
   possible with embedded circulations today.

   Otherwise, elevated thunderstorms will remain possible from the
   Edwards Plateau into interior south TX in a moist environment with
   ascent and weak buoyancy atop the cooler near-surface air mass.

   ...Pacific Northwest and the lower Great Lakes...
   The potential for isolated lightning flashes with low-topped
   convection will diminish across northwest WA by about midday as a
   midlevel trough moves inland and height rises ensue.  A separate
   midlevel trough will continue southeastward over the lower Great
   Lakes by this evening into early tonight.  Cooling midlevel
   temperatures and weak buoyancy aided by the relatively warm lakes
   will support convection that could become sufficiently deep to
   support charge separation and isolated lightning flashes.

   ..Thompson/Barnes.. 11/08/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 080656

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1256 AM CST Sun Nov 08 2026

   Valid 091200Z - 101200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe thunderstorms are forecast across the U.S. Monday and
   Monday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   Mid-level west-northwesterly flow will be in place across much of
   the central and eastern U.S. on Monday. Further south, an
   upper-level low will move across the southern High Plains, weakening
   substantially during the day. Southeastward from the low, scattered
   thunderstorms will be possible early in the day over parts of south
   Texas. Instability will be very weak and no severe threat is
   expected. Elsewhere, thunderstorms are not forecast across the
   continental U.S. Monday and Monday night.

   ..Broyles.. 11/08/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

SPC AC 080822

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0222 AM CST Sun Nov 08 2026

   Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe threat is forecast across the U.S. Tuesday and Tuesday
   night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   At mid-levels, a shortwave trough will move across the north-central
   U.S. on Tuesday, as west-northwesterly flow remains in place over
   much of the central and eastern U.S. A shortwave trough will also
   move eastward in the vicinity of the western Gulf Coast. Isolated
   thunderstorms will be possible within a moist airmass from south
   Texas to the middle Texas Coast on Tuesday. No severe threat is
   expected, and thunderstorms are not forecast across the remainder of
   the continental U.S. Tuesday and Tuesday night.

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
